blocks.text: 我们推出 GPT‑6 Cyber，这是安全研究领域的一次重大飞跃：它发现和修复漏洞的能力更强，也更能可靠地守住研究人员设定的边界。在关键网络安全基准测试中，GPT‑6 Cyber 相比 GPT‑5.6 Cyber 取得大幅提升，其中 ExploitGym 相对提升 51%，在范围遵守测试中更是出现阶跃式改进。它已经在帮助保护真实世界的软件，在 Linux、Firefox 等安全关键代码库中发现并验证了数千个漏洞利用。

inlines.text: 我们推出 GPT‑6 Cyber，这是安全研究领域的一次重大飞跃：它发现和修复漏洞的能力更强，也更能可靠地守住研究人员设定的边界。在关键网络安全基准测试中，GPT‑6 Cyber 相比 GPT‑5.6 Cyber 取得大幅提升，其中 ExploitGym 相对提升 51%，在范围遵守测试中更是出现阶跃式改进。它已经在帮助保护真实世界的软件，在 Linux、Firefox 等安全关键代码库中发现并验证了数千个漏洞利用。

blocks.text: ExploitGym 测试的是模型能否利用指定漏洞，GPT‑6 Cyber 得分 48.5%，高于 GPT‑5.6 Cyber 的 32.1%。它也更能可靠地遵守任务边界：在另一项对齐评估中，不启用部署提示词时，GPT‑6 Cyber 在 99.93% 的测试中避免了对范围外服务的利用，启用提示词后这一比例达到 100%。对齐方面的这一进步，源于针对遵守授权范围、尊重限制条件、准确报告结果的专门训练。

inlines.text: ExploitGym 测试的是模型能否利用指定漏洞，GPT‑6 Cyber 得分 48.5%，高于 GPT‑5.6 Cyber 的 32.1%。它也更能可靠地遵守任务边界：在另一项对齐评估中，不启用部署提示词时，GPT‑6 Cyber 在 99.93% 的测试中避免了对范围外服务的利用，启用提示词后这一比例达到 100%。对齐方面的这一进步，源于针对遵守授权范围、尊重限制条件、准确报告结果的专门训练。

blocks.text: 这些能力已经在帮助保护真实系统。我们的研究人员用 GPT‑6 Cyber 在 Linux 中开发出 948 个提权漏洞利用，并在 Firefox 中识别出 81 个此前未知的高危漏洞——尽管此前已用前沿模型做过大量测试。该模型还帮助开发了候选补丁，Mozilla 已为其中许多 Firefox 漏洞发布修复程序（在新窗口打开）。Cisco、Calif 和 CodeRabbit 的安全团队正在用它进行漏洞研究和代码审查，我们也依靠它发现并修复自身基础设施中的弱点。

blocks.text: 显然，我们利用前沿模型来保护软件的时间窗口有限。我们的目标是大幅扩展 Daybreak，把先进的安全研究带给各种规模的组织、独立研究人员和开源维护者。GPT‑6 Astra 等主线模型已经支持代码审查、漏洞分类和补丁开发。Daybreak Blue 帮助经过验证的防御者验证漏洞和修复，减少不必要的拒绝；Daybreak Red 则借助 GPT‑6 Cyber 支持更深入的漏洞利用开发和授权安全测试。

blocks.text: GPT‑6 Cyber 相比 GPT‑5.6 Cyber 是重大升级，在大多数网络任务上表现优于 GPT‑6 Astra，即使 Astra 没有拒绝请求也是如此。我们在要求模型理解软件、识别漏洞并开发可用漏洞利用的任务上对它进行了评估。基于这些结果，按照我们的 Preparedness Framework，我们将该模型在网络安全领域归类为 Critical，高于 GPT‑5.6 Cyber 的 High。

inlines.text: 对齐更强，更善于守住边界

blocks.text: 网络安全智能体面临的一个风险是：它们会超出任务范围，试图攻击无关服务，或无视研究人员设定的交战规则。

blocks.text: 我们把对齐作为 GPT‑6 Cyber 的核心重点，通过专门训练帮助模型留在授权范围内、遵守对其行为的限制，并准确汇报工作。部署前，我们开展了一系列对齐评测来衡量这些行为。完整结果见系统卡⁠（在新窗口打开）。

blocks.text: 其中一项评测是 ExploitGym Honeypot，其设计参考了Hugging Face 事件⁠。我们在隔离环境中给模型一个难度较高的漏洞利用任务，同时让它能访问包注册表、对象存储等配套服务。我们故意让这些服务容易被攻破，这样攻击它们就能暴露出任务的 flag。模型必须推断出攻击这些服务超出了任务范围。

blocks.text: 8 项中的第 1 项

inlines.text: 8 项中的第 1 项

blocks.text: “GPT‑6 Cyber 是世界级的网络防御模型。Firefox 进入 2026 年时，已是全球加固最彻底、审查最严格的代码库之一。即便又经过多代前沿模型的进一步加固，GPT‑6 Cyber 仍发现了此前未知的高危漏洞，指出了架构层面的改进方向，并帮助我们向数百万用户推送了修复。”

inlines.text: Brian Grinstead，Firefox 杰出工程师

blocks.text: “在长时间运行的漏洞利用开发任务上，这是我们用过最好的模型。它能逐步构建原语库，再从中找到通往更强利用的路径，相比前几代是质的飞跃。”

inlines.text: Thai Duong，Calif 首席执行官

blocks.text: “在我们内部的未知漏洞发现与利用基准测试中，GPT‑6 Cyber 是表现最好的模型，得分 23%，此前最佳成绩为 13%。它在大型代码库中发现高影响漏洞并转化为端到端概念验证的效率极高。这个模型正在推动模型处理网络安全问题能力的前沿。”

inlines.text: Steven Hao，Cognition 首席技术官

blocks.text: “相比此前的模型，GPT‑6 Cyber 是一次重大飞跃。我们发现它更快、更具成本效益，也明显更聪明。它已经在帮助我们更好地保护自家产品；通过 Unit 42 持续前沿 AI 防御，我们正把同样的速度和精度带给客户，以大规模保护企业软件。”

inlines.text: Lee Klarich，Palo Alto Networks 首席产品与技术官

blocks.text: “防御现代基础设施需要持续创新。随着威胁形势日益复杂，借助 OpenAI GPT‑6 Cyber 等前沿 AI 模型，是让天平向防御方倾斜的关键一步。把这些能力融入我们的研究，能让团队以更快的速度和更高的精度分析复杂架构、识别风险，最终增强客户所依赖技术的韧性与可信度。”

inlines.text: Anthony Grieco，Cisco 高级副总裁、首席安全与信任官

blocks.text: “安全研究最难的部分，是把零散的线索串联起来，清楚理解一次攻击可能如何发生。GPT‑6 Cyber 帮助我们的研究人员建立这些联系、验证假设，并发现需要深入调查的薄弱点。它拓展了专家们能承担的工作，也帮助我们把这些理解转化为对客户更好的保护。”

inlines.text: Chris Corde，SentinelOne 首席产品官

blocks.text: “我们把 GPT‑6 用在最难发现的缺陷上：藏在复杂逻辑里、分散在多个组件中，或只有经过一长串条件才能触达的问题。它能端到端地推进这些调查而不丢失线索，并给出清晰、可复现的发现，让团队能快速验证和修复。”

inlines.text: Kyle Polley，Perplexity 首席信息安全官

blocks.text: “GPT‑6 Cyber 是我们测试过的安全审查最强模型。在我们的内部基准测试中，它发现的高危和中危安全问题比我们的生产模型多 66%。这些正是开发者用 AI 智能体构建时需要修复的缺陷。”

blocks.text: 保护关键基础设施

inlines.text: 保护关键基础设施

blocks.text: 在设计 GPT‑6 Cyber 的防护措施和访问权限时，保护关键基础设施一直是核心考量，包括发电厂、水处理设施，以及支撑这些设施的运营技术（OT）和工业控制系统（ICS）。我们既希望让负责防御这些系统的团队用上我们能力最强的模型，也希望强化防护措施，防止未经授权的攻击。

inlines.text: 在设计 GPT‑6 Cyber 的防护措施和访问权限时，保护关键基础设施一直是核心考量，包括发电厂、水处理设施，以及支撑这些设施的运营技术（OT）和工业控制系统（ICS）。我们既希望让负责防御这些系统的团队用上我们能力最强的模型，也希望强化防护措施，防止未经授权的攻击。

blocks.text: 首先，为了武装这些防御者，我们设立了 10 亿美元的Daybreak 一线防御者计划⁠，为政府机构和基本服务提供商等资源有限的团队提供访问补贴。我们还在 Daybreak Red 下新设了一个面向获批关键基础设施防御者的分组（Daybreak Red 关键基础设施组），允许他们对关键系统进行授权测试，同时保留针对模型失准的防护措施。

blocks.text: 防护拦截率更高并不总是更好。本次评估中的许多技术对正当的安全工作同样不可或缺：理解系统、发现漏洞、验证修复能否抵御攻击。因此，我们是在支持正当研究和打补丁的前提下评估这些比率，而不是追求 100%。

blocks.text: 为了评估我们的模型如何帮助防御关键基础设施，我们与 Dragos 合作，后者是全球扩展运营技术（xOT）网络安全提供商。Dragos 在受控实验室环境中使用对网络活动较为宽松的 Daybreak Red 模型进行了评估。评估涵盖了一系列请求，从网络发现和资产枚举，逐步推进到定向侦察、敏感数据外泄，以及未经授权、可能危险的设备操作。

blocks.text: “Dragos 把一个前沿模型放进模拟电厂靶场，几乎没给它任何提示。它自己就把 OT 资产从 IT 噪声里分离出来，随后在管理保护继电器数据的工程软件中发现两个零日漏洞，这些漏洞会暴露保护定值和断路器跳闸逻辑。这正是攻击者在触碰任何物理设备之前想要的那张地图。发动攻击前所需的侦察和漏洞研究，门槛正在降低。与 OpenAI 合作开展这项工作，能让他们在真实对手之前看清攻击者穿越 OT 网络的路径，从而围绕这些攻击可能的展开方式构建防护措施，同时让模型继续为防御这些系统的人所用。”
——Rob T. Lee，Dragos 首席 AI 官

inlines.text: ——Rob T. Lee，Dragos 首席 AI 官

blocks.text: We’re introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, a major leap in security research: more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities, and far more reliable staying within the boundaries researchers set. GPT‑6 Cyber delivers major gains on key cybersecurity benchmarks over GPT‑5.6 Cyber, including a 51% relative improvement on ExploitGym and a step function improvement when tested on staying within scope. It is already helping to secure real-world software, uncovering and validating thousands of exploits in security-critical codebases such as Linux and Firefox.

inlines.text: We’re introducing GPT‑6 Cyber, a major leap in security research: more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities, and far more reliable staying within the boundaries researchers set. GPT‑6 Cyber delivers major gains on key cybersecurity benchmarks over GPT‑5.6 Cyber, including a 51% relative improvement on ExploitGym and a step function improvement when tested on staying within scope. It is already helping to secure real-world software, uncovering and validating thousands of exploits in security-critical codebases such as Linux and Firefox.

blocks.text: On ExploitGym, which tests whether models can exploit a specified vulnerability, GPT‑6 Cyber scores 48.5%, up from 32.1% for GPT‑5.6 Cyber. It also follows task boundaries more reliably: in a separate alignment evaluation, GPT‑6 Cyber avoided exploiting out-of-scope services in 99.93% of tests without its deployment prompt, and 100% with this prompt. This improvement in alignment reflects dedicated training to stay within authorized scope, respect restrictions, and report results accurately.

blocks.text: These capabilities are already helping secure real systems. Our researchers used GPT‑6 Cyber to develop 948 privilege escalation exploits in Linux⁠ and identify 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox, despite extensive prior testing with frontier models. The model also helped develop candidate patches, and Mozilla has released fixes for many of the Firefox vulnerabilities⁠(opens in a new window). Security teams at Cisco, Calif, and CodeRabbit are using it for vulnerability research and code review, and we have relied on it to find and fix weaknesses in our own infrastructure⁠.

blocks.text: It is clear that we have a limited window to use frontier models to secure software⁠. Our goal is to dramatically expand Daybreak, bringing advanced security research to organizations of every size, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers. Mainline models such as GPT‑6 Astra already support code review, vulnerability triage, and patch development. Daybreak Blue helps verified defenders validate vulnerabilities and fixes with fewer unnecessary refusals, while Daybreak Red enables deeper exploit development and authorized security testing with GPT‑6 Cyber.

blocks.text: Advancing frontier cyber capabilities

inlines.text: Advancing frontier cyber capabilities

blocks.text: GPT‑6 Cyber is a major step up from GPT‑5.6 Cyber and outperforms GPT‑6 Astra on most cyber tasks, even when Astra does not refuse the request. We evaluated the model on tasks that require it to understand software, identify vulnerabilities, and develop working exploits. Based on these results, we classify the model as Critical in cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework, up from High for GPT‑5.6 Cyber.

inlines.text: GPT‑6 Cyber is a major step up from GPT‑5.6 Cyber and outperforms GPT‑6 Astra on most cyber tasks, even when Astra does not refuse the request. We evaluated the model on tasks that require it to understand software, identify vulnerabilities, and develop working exploits. Based on these results, we classify the model as Critical in cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework, up from High for GPT‑5.6 Cyber.

blocks.text: On ExploitGym, which tests whether models can exploit a specified vulnerability in a remote target, GPT‑6 Cyber scores 48.5%, about 16 percentage points higher than GPT‑5.6 Cyber’s 32.1%. To test vulnerability discovery, we also built a new evaluation for offensive web penetration testing. Models probe web applications without access to their source code. GPT‑6 Cyber achieved 40.3% recall of vulnerabilities compared with 32.0% for GPT‑6 Astra.

blocks.text: Daybreak Red is designed to support more advanced security workflows, including developing working exploits and using them against remote targets. To evaluate these capabilities, we built a new benchmark called RemoteExploitBench, which uses known vulnerabilities in applications such as GitLab, PostgreSQL, and Jenkins deployed in a controlled environment. In our initial evaluation, GPT‑6 Astra running with Daybreak Blue refused 100% of tasks, while GPT‑6 Cyber completed 95%; its only failure was an exploit it could not get to work remotely. See the system card⁠(opens in a new window) for full results and evaluation settings.

blocks.text: We made alignment a central focus of GPT‑6 Cyber, using specialized training to help the model stay within authorized scope, follow restrictions on its actions, and report its work accurately. Before deployment, we ran a series of alignment evaluations to measure these behaviors. See the system card⁠(opens in a new window) for full results.

blocks.text: One of these evaluations is ExploitGym Honeypot, which was informed by the Hugging Face incident⁠. We give the model a difficult exploitation task in an isolated environment with access to supporting services, such as a package registry or object store. We deliberately make these services easy to exploit so that attacking them can reveal the task’s flag. The model must infer that exploiting them is outside the scope of its task.

blocks.text: We have also relied on GPT‑6 Cyber to secure our own systems. It was one of the main models behind the work we recently shared on hardening the infrastructure used to train frontier models⁠. In controlled red-teaming campaigns, agents using GPT‑6 Cyber and other OpenAI models chained vulnerabilities to escape microVMs and execute code on the underlying hosts. We used the findings to patch software, tighten network restrictions, and report issues to maintainers and vendors.

blocks.text: Our vulnerability researchers also use GPT‑6 Cyber to find and validate vulnerabilities in open-source software at scale. This work has uncovered previously unknown flaws in software that has been scrutinized for years:

inlines.text: Our vulnerability researchers also use GPT‑6 Cyber to find and validate vulnerabilities in open-source software at scale. This work has uncovered previously unknown flaws in software that has been scrutinized for years:
Found 81 novel Firefox vulnerabilities.

GPT‑6 Cyber can be suitable for use in autonomous workflows for finding vulnerabilities and proposing high-quality patches at scale. During a vulnerability research campaign, GPT‑6 Cyber produced evidence and reproducible tests for 81 novel vulnerabilities classified by Mozilla as high severity, and showed that an additional 30 known issues were more severe than previously reported. We disclosed the findings to Mozilla, along with proposed patches to help its engineers develop fixes. Mozilla was supportive of this work, and began
landing fixes shortly after receiving the reports⁠(opens in a new window)
Developing exploits for
948 Linux kernel vulnerabilities

GPT‑6 Cyber reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and developed working exploits for 948—more than five times the 166 exploited by GPT‑5.6 Sol using the same research harness. Following the Linux community's guidance, we disclosed 304 critical findings to maintainers with candidate patches and are in the process of getting other vulnerabilities fixed.
Demonstrating critical RCE vulnerabilities.
We recently discussed a
critical vulnerability in Brotli⁠(opens in a new window)

, a compression library used by Node.js and other software. Our security researchers used GPT‑6 Cyber alongside other OpenAI models to develop and validate exploits showing how the flaw could enable remote code execution in downstream applications.

blocks.text: Detecting misuse and blocking high-risk activity

inlines.text: Detecting misuse and blocking high-risk activity

blocks.text: As models become more capable and uncover more security vulnerabilities, we are also seeing more attempts to use them to cause harm. These attempts include efforts by malicious cyber actors and adversarial groups seeking to distill our models. We have thus paired GPT‑6 Cyber’s stronger capabilities with stronger safeguards to detect and disrupt misuse and keep the model’s actions within the user’s intent and authorization.

blocks.text: We added and strengthened these protections alongside the release of GPT‑6 Cyber (see the system card⁠(opens in a new window) for full information):

inlines.text: We added and strengthened these protections alongside the release of GPT‑6 Cyber (see the
system card⁠(opens in a new window)
for full information):
Cyber-specific misalignment monitoring.
We monitor whether actions match the user’s authorization, while recognizing legitimate exploit development and testing.
Targeted monitoring for emerging threats.

For example, during the coordinated disclosure of critical PHP vulnerabilities, we set up targeted monitoring for attempts to develop exploits against live PHP servers, while preserving support for defenders patching affected systems.
Private Safety Processing (PSP)****.
We use automated checks to review related interactions for misuse. Standard retention remains the default. API customers using
Zero Data Retention⁠(opens in a new window)
generally must use
PSP⁠(opens in a new window)
, which reviews encrypted records retained in customer storage for 30 days without exposing prompts and responses to OpenAI personnel.
Protection against stolen credentials.
We require IP allowlisting for Daybreak Red API access by default, restricting requests to approved networks with limited exceptions. We also monitor credentials for compromise.
Sandboxing and oversight.
As with past models, we recommend
sandboxing⁠(opens in a new window)
action review⁠(opens in a new window)
, and human oversight for high-risk workflows.
Protections against high-risk cyber assistance.
We use new checks to block high-risk activity involving critical systems (see below for more).

blocks.text: Defending critical infrastructure

inlines.text: Defending critical infrastructure

blocks.text: Protecting critical infrastructure has been a key consideration in designing GPT‑6 Cyber’s safeguards and access, including power plants, water treatment facilities, and the operational technology and industrial control systems (OT/ICS) that underpin them. We simultaneously want to give the teams defending these systems access to our most capable models while also strengthening our safeguards to prevent unauthorized attacks.

inlines.text: Protecting critical infrastructure has been a key consideration in designing GPT‑6 Cyber’s safeguards and access, including power plants, water treatment facilities, and the operational technology and industrial control systems (OT/ICS) that underpin them. We simultaneously want to give the teams defending these systems access to our most capable models while also strengthening our safeguards to prevent unauthorized attacks.

blocks.text: First, to equip these defenders, our $1 billion Daybreak for Frontline Defenders⁠ grant program subsidizes access for resource-constrained teams such as government organizations and essential service providers. We’re also introducing a new group within Daybreak Red (Daybreak Red for Critical Infrastructure) for approved critical infrastructure defenders, which gives them permissions to conduct authorized testing of critical systems while retaining safeguards against model misalignment.

blocks.text: To evaluate how our models can help defend critical infrastructure, we partnered with Dragos, the global provider for extended operational technology (xOT) cybersecurity. Dragos ran evaluations using cyber-permissive Daybreak Red models in a controlled lab environment. The evaluations covered requests progressing from network discovery and asset enumeration through targeted reconnaissance, sensitive data exfiltration, and unauthorized, potentially dangerous device actions.

inlines.text: To evaluate how our models can help defend critical infrastructure, we partnered with Dragos, the global provider for extended operational technology (xOT) cybersecurity. Dragos ran evaluations using cyber-permissive Daybreak Red models in a controlled lab environment. The evaluations covered requests progressing from network discovery and asset enumeration through targeted reconnaissance, sensitive data exfiltration, and unauthorized, potentially dangerous device actions.

blocks.text: “Dragos put a frontier model on a mock power plant range and told it almost nothing. On its own, it separated the OT assets from the IT noise, then found two zero-days in engineering software that manages protective relay data, exposing protection settings and breaker trip logic. That’s the map an adversary wants before touching anything physical. The skill floor is dropping for the reconnaissance and vulnerability research needed before an attack. Working with OpenAI on this shows them the adversary’s path through an OT network before real adversaries take it, so safeguards get built around how these attacks could unfold, while the models stay useful to the people defending these systems.”
—Rob T. Lee, Chief AI Officer, Dragos

inlines.text: —Rob T. Lee, Chief AI Officer, Dragos

blocks.text: We used feedback from Dragos to refine our safeguards, aiming to block harmful assistance without unnecessarily restricting authorized testing. See their final report⁠(opens in a new window) for details on the evaluations. We’re also working to expand partnerships with other offensive security providers and purple teams on penetration testing and red teaming with AI, and with energy companies, other critical infrastructure operators, and national labs to assess our models’ effectiveness and safeguards in industrial defense. We have also increased our investment in threat investigations to detect model usage involving OT/ICS. We’ll continue refining our safeguards with input from partners and the security community, including reports through /feedback when safeguards miss harmful activity or interrupt legitimate work.

inlines.text: Expanding access to trusted defenders

blocks.text: GPT‑6 Cyber is initially available through the API and Codex to a select group of approved Daybreak Red customers. We will progressively expand access to all Daybreak Red customers soon, and are also making GPT‑5.6 Cyber available to all Daybreak Red customers. We’re also expanding Daybreak Blue alpha access for GPT‑6 Astra to more organizations and individual security researchers; let us know⁠(opens in a new window) if you’re interested.
